content_voiceover: This table covers leukoreduction and irradiation requirements across blood products, high-yield for boards. Red cells and platelets both need a standard blood set, should be leukoreduced to reduce febrile reactions, HLA alloimmunization, and CMV risk, and both need irradiation to prevent transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease, especially for stem cell transplant recipients. Plasma and cryoprecipitate need a standard set, but leukoreduction doesn't apply and irradiation isn't needed, since they're essentially acellular. Granulocyte concentrates need a standard set, cannot be leukoreduced, since that would remove the white cells you're giving, and almost always need irradiation because they're loaded with viable lymphocytes. Hematopoietic stem cells are the outlier, no standard set needed, cannot be leukoreduced, and absolutely cannot be irradiated, since that would kill the very stem cells you're transplanting. One footnote, cellular therapy products resemble stem cells but vary by manufacturer, so confirm handling with the supplier.
keypoints: RBCs and platelets: leukoreduce and irradiate, especially for transplant recipients
Plasma and cryoprecipitate: no leukoreduction, no irradiation needed
Granulocyte concentrates cannot be leukoreduced but almost always need irradiation
Hematopoietic stem cells can never be irradiated or leukoreduced
Irradiation across products prevents transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease
keypoint_voiceover: Quick recall, RBCs and platelets get both leukoreduced and irradiated. Plasma and cryoprecipitate need neither, they're acellular. Granulocytes can never be leukoreduced, but almost always need irradiation because they're full of live lymphocytes. And stem cells are the exception that can never be irradiated, since that would kill the graft you're trying to infuse. Irradiation across the board exists to prevent Ta-GVHD.
